_comment: Mutation sweep for V-BRK-032 -- every key the agent puts on the wire is a key the broker's decoder accepts. Run: python3 dev/mutate.py verification/mutants/V-BRK-032.json. Every row names the test that must fail; see dev/mutate.py for why rc != 0 is not a catch. Only the platform tier is mutated: the three copies are byte-identical and each is read separately, so a mutation in one is a mutation the check must see.

mutants.why: THE defect this check exists for. `broker.Trace` has no parent, DecodeEnvelope disallows unknown fields, and every action in a traced session comes back 400 naming a trace key.
A capital D. Unknown on the way in and absent on the way out, so it must trip the unknown-key property AND the required-field one -- a misspelling is not a rename.
`nonce` carries no omitempty, so the broker expects it on every envelope. Dropping it is the other direction, and it is invisible to an unknown-key check.
`requireApproval` sits in a conditional branch, which is where parentSpanId hid. A key only some envelopes carry is a key only some envelopes are refused for.

Not a defect in the agent: a defect in this check's premise. With DisallowUnknownFields gone every decode below passes for a reason unrelated to the agent being right, and the sweep must notice that the measurement died rather than that the code got better.
The same string, but reached through a variable so a text grep for it in the assignment would miss. The AST-scoped literal check is what has to see this.
